source: NCERT Class X, Contemporary India II, Geography Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Minerals — Basics
points: A **mineral** is a homogeneous, naturally occurring substance with a definable internal structure; found in **ores** (accumulation of minerals mixed with other elements).

Occurrence: in **veins/lodes** (igneous/metamorphic rocks), **beds/layers** (sedimentary, e.g. coal, gypsum), by **decomposition** of surface rocks (bauxite), in **placer deposits** (sands of valley floors, e.g. gold), and in **ocean waters**.

Classified into **metallic** (ferrous like iron/manganese; non-ferrous like copper, bauxite; precious like gold/silver) and **non-metallic** (mica, limestone) and **energy** minerals (coal, petroleum).

sections.heading: 2. Major Metallic Minerals
points: **Iron ore** — backbone of industry; **magnetite** (best, highest iron content ~70%) and **hematite** (most important commercially). Belts: Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Ballari-Chitradurga (Karnataka), Maharashtra-Goa.
**Manganese** — used in steel making and ferro alloys; Odisha is largest producer.
**Copper** — malleable, good conductor (electricals); Khetri (Rajasthan), Balaghat (MP), Singhbhum (Jharkhand).
**Bauxite** — ore of **aluminium**; found in Amarkantak plateau, Bilaspur-Katni; Odisha largest producer.

sections.heading: 3. Non-Metallic Minerals
points: **Mica** — a key mineral for the electrical/electronics industry (insulator); found in Jharkhand (Koderma-Hazaribagh belt = finest mica), Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh.
**Limestone** — basic raw material for **cement** and iron smelting.
Rat-hole mining (e.g. Meghalaya) and unsafe mining are hazards for workers and environment.

sections.heading: 4. Energy Resources — Conventional and Non-Conventional
points: **Conventional:** coal (most abundant fossil fuel — Gondwana coal: Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro; Tertiary coal in NE), petroleum ('black gold' — Mumbai High, Gujarat, Assam-Digboi), natural gas, and hydel power.
**Non-conventional (renewable):** solar, wind (Jaisalmer; India has large wind farms), tidal (Gulf of Kachchh), geothermal (Parvati valley, Puga valley Ladakh), biogas.
India promotes **solar and wind** energy for sustainability; conservation of energy is essential (use of public transport, energy-efficient devices).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Magnetite = highest iron content (~70%); hematite = most commercially important.
Bauxite = ore of aluminium; copper = Khetri (Rajasthan).
Finest mica = Koderma-Hazaribagh (Jharkhand).
Gondwana coal = Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro; petroleum = 'black gold' (Mumbai High, Digboi).
Tidal energy = Gulf of Kachchh; geothermal = Puga valley (Ladakh), Parvati valley.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Magnetite** has the **highest iron content**; **bauxite** is the ore of **aluminium** (not iron).
**Mica** is a **non-metallic** mineral vital for **electronics** (best in Koderma, Jharkhand).
**Petroleum** is called **'black gold'**; **Digboi (Assam)** was an early oil field.
**Coal** is the **most abundant** fossil fuel in India.
